data.body:
LIVE ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE — GitHub Actions run 30651750699, job "jira DC harness smoke (real Jira Data
Center, ephemeral)", on merged commit 132a0f9dc (this fix).

RESULT: **1 failed, 14 passed in 15.67s — and ZERO `UserTokenLimitExceededException`.**

Before this fix the same job died at SETUP:

    ERROR at setup of test_add_label_and_the_links_surface_against_a_real_instance
    AssertionError: PAT creation failed: 403
      {'exception': 'com.atlassian.pats.exception.UserTokenLimitExceededException'}

reproduced across runs 30604756524 and 30623000498. In this run no test errors at setup and the PAT
exception does not appear anywhere in the job log (verified by targeted grep over the full log, not
by reading the summary line).

AGAINST THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
 * "the full suite runs with ZERO UserTokenLimitExceededException, confirmed by reading THAT JOB's log
   rather than the overall run status" — MET. I read the job. Note the RUN is red, for reasons that
   have nothing to do with this fix (see below); reading the run status would have given the wrong
   answer in both directions.
 * "headroom is structural, not coincidental" — MET, and this is the part worth stating precisely.
   The suite did not squeak under the cap: session scope makes consumption O(1) in test count, so ONE
   PAT is minted per run regardless of how many tests request it. That is why 15 collected tests pass
   where 11 previously exhausted the budget, and why J11 can add substantially more without
   re-approaching it.
 * the leftover-token sweep did not fire here and could not have: the CI harness is an EPHEMERAL
   container built fresh by `docker compose up --build`, so no run can inherit another's tokens. Its
   value is for a persistent/local instance, and it is covered by unit tests against a stubbed
   `_request` rather than by this run. Recording that explicitly so the sweep is not mistaken for
   live-proven by this evidence.

WHAT THE ONE FAILURE IS — NOT THIS FIX, AND IMPORTANT
`test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` failed with:

    AssertionError: no local ticket was created from DC issue RBJNAZV-1
    stdout='invariants: scanned=1 filed=0 (cap=5)\nOK: applied 1 of 1 mutations\n'

That is a genuine INBOUND defect, and it is only visible because this fix let the suite run at all.
Compare the last recorded live run, which reported `scanned=0` and "converged" — it converged because
the store was empty. Here `scanned=1`: the pass SEES the DC issue and reports applying a mutation, yet
`filed=0` and no local ticket exists. That is epic e369's headline acceptance criterion ("an issue
created in DC appears in the local store after an inbound pass") failing for a real, mechanical
reason. Filed separately; not in this ticket's scope.

Two defects had been masking it in sequence: the PAT cap killed the run at setup, and before that an
empty store made "converged" indistinguishable from "works".

ALSO IN THIS RUN, AND UNRELATED: the "external integration (live services)" job failed two LLM tests
(`test_single_turn_live_structured_output`, `test_live_plan_review_workflow_engine_produces_real_verdict`
— the latter on `llm_ran is False`). That is the live-model tier, a different job with different
inputs; it touches neither the DC harness nor this fix.
